method.name: System Decomposition
method.does: Break the system into the seven layers; define agent capabilities, goals and interactions.

method.name: Layer-Specific Threat Modeling
method.does: Use each layer's threat landscape, tailored to the system.

method.name: Risk Assessment
method.does: Assess likelihood and impact and prioritize. The article refers to a risk matrix but does not define one.

method.name: Implementation and Monitoring
method.does: Implement, monitor and update the model as the system evolves.

notes: Layer names and threat labels are quoted from the CSA article. Secondary write-ups name some layers differently; this lab follows the article.
The article's threat lists are a starting point to be tailored to the system (its step 2). A threat that is not in the list is allowed here, and is marked custom.
Several Layer 6 threats are about AI security agents. AcmeBank has none, so a learner must say so rather than force a label.

CSA also lists a MAESTRO v2 artifact. Its listing describes a peer-review draft that grows the model from seven layers to ten in three operational domains; its page could not be fetched on 2026-10-29. This lab follows the original seven-layer article, and v2 is NOT implemented.

analyzer.name: MAESTRO Threat Analyzer
analyzer.provenance_note: The README calls it the official CSA repository, while the page header shows a fork and the CSA labs page links a different GitHub account. Verify before relying on it.
analyzer.inputs: A free-text description of the system architecture, plus presets.
analyzer.outputs: For each of the seven layers: traditional threats and agentic threats, each with generated mitigations. No likelihood, impact, severity, register or export format is documented.
analyzer.uses_llm: Yes (Genkit with Google, OpenAI or Ollama); output varies run to run.
analyzer.status_here: NOT RUN. It needs Node.js and a model provider, and its output is generated text. This lab reuses its output structure (traditional versus agentic threats per layer, with mitigations) and gives you an architecture description to paste into it yourself.
compare: Paste the architecture description from your report into the Analyzer, in your own environment and with your own provider.
For each layer, list the threats it proposes that your register lacks, and the ones in your register it did not propose.
Treat every Analyzer threat as a hypothesis: find the AgentSecLab component, the control and the evidence, or mark it NOT PROVEN.

risk_method.why: The article asks for likelihood and impact and a risk matrix but defines none. This lab reuses the Risk Center's qualitative 3x3 matrix. A level is looked up from two judgments you enter; the tool never proposes them.

example.scope: AcmeBank's lending-policy assistant: a customer-operations user asks for a policy summary and the agent may perform only explicitly authorized supporting lookups. In scope: the application, the model, retrieval, memory, tools, the optional gateway, telemetry and Splunk. Out of scope: real customers, authentication (NOT MODELED), human approval (NOT MODELED), cryptographic delegation (NOT MODELED), any production system.

register.label: Adversarial Examples
register.description: Crafted text in an application note or retrieved document steers the model's proposal (prompt injection).

inherent.rationale: On the labelled vulnerable profile the planted text passes; a model is not a policy engine.

register.mitigation: Treat model output as an untrusted proposal; decide outside the model; constrain what an allowed tool may carry (argument-level allow-list).

residual.rationale: Controls hold for the lab's fixtures; semantic resistance outside them is NOT PROVEN.

register.label: Compromised RAG Pipelines
register.description: A retrieved document carries an instruction the agent follows.

inherent.rationale: Retrieved content enters the context as data but can still influence the agent.

register.mitigation: Keep retrieved text as data; authorize every follow-on tool request independently; add a purpose check on retrieval.

residual.rationale: The context control only observes: influence can remain even when authority is denied.

register.label: Data Poisoning
register.description: A persisted memory entry poisons a later run.

inherent.rationale: A write in one run is recalled in another with no user present.

register.mitigation: Validate on write, classify on recall, bind memory to an owner, and authorize any follow-on tool request.

residual.rationale: Recall classification observes only; ownership and deletion are NOT MEASURED.

register.label: Data Exfiltration
register.description: A tool result or preview exposes more customer data than the task needed.

inherent.rationale: Authorizing a tool call is not authorizing the data it returns.

register.mitigation: Minimize what a tool returns; bound previews; authorize resources, not just tools.

residual.rationale: Synthetic data only; real data handling is outside the lab.

register.label: Input Validation Attacks
register.description: Malformed, oversized or duplicate-key requests reach the HTTP boundary.

inherent.rationale: Any caller can send any bytes to an HTTP endpoint.

register.mitigation: Closed request contracts, strict JSON that refuses duplicate keys, size limits, errors before any handler.

residual.rationale: The recorded runs show refusal for the shapes tested; other shapes are not tested.

register.label: Supply Chain Attacks
register.description: Third-party tool metadata or a dependency carries a hostile instruction or code.

inherent.rationale: Descriptions are read by the agent; dependencies run in the service.

register.mitigation: Treat metadata as data; pin and inventory components; never let provenance stand in for a grant.

residual.rationale: Inventory is not trust; scanner findings are not authorization.

register.label: Compromised Container Images
register.description: The Ollama image is pulled by a floating tag, so a re-pushed image changes the model runtime silently.

inherent.rationale: docker-compose.yml uses ollama/ollama:latest; no digest was measured.

register.mitigation: Pin by digest (deploy/images.lock.json with require_digests) and verify after pull.

residual.rationale: NOT RESOLVED: the pin is not enforced for Ollama.

register.label: Lateral Movement
register.description: Anything that reaches the container network can call AcmeBank and the Attack Service, which authenticate no callers themselves.
register.mitigation: Do not publish service ports; keep the gateway as the only entry; add service-to-service authentication and network policy.

residual.rationale: The gateway narrows exposure but inside the network trust remains; service authentication is not implemented.

register.label: Evasion of Detection
register.description: A fail-open ALLOW raises no alert, so silence is read as safety.

inherent.rationale: The lab's detector alerts only on a DENY followed by a handler start.

register.mitigation: Hunt for the allowed-but-unexpected case as well; never treat a zero-row result as a DENY or as SAFE.

residual.rationale: Detection is downstream; it prevents nothing.

register.label: Data Leakage through Observability
register.description: Telemetry is a second copy of runtime events; anything placed in an event is readable by whoever can search the index.

inherent.rationale: Event content and index access are separate decisions.

register.mitigation: Put hashes and identifiers in events rather than raw content; restrict who can search the index.

residual.rationale: Synthetic data only; index access control is the operator's.

register.label: Poisoning Observability Data
register.description: Forged or altered telemetry makes an investigation reach the wrong conclusion.

inherent.rationale: Events are copies; the lab does not sign them.

register.mitigation: Sign or hash events at the source; compare the local pack with the indexed copy; keep the local pack as the source of truth.

residual.rationale: No control exists today. NOT PROVEN either way.

register.label: Policy and allow-ticket tampering
register.description: Changing the coded policy, or forging an allow ticket, changes every authorization decision. (Custom: the article's Layer 6 threats concern AI security agents, and AcmeBank has none.)

inherent.rationale: Policy is code; execution needs an opaque ticket minted after ALLOW.

register.mitigation: Protect code and image integrity; pin tests on the coded grants; keep the decision point small.

residual.rationale: Integrity of the code and the image is only as strong as the supply chain (EX-T06, EX-T07).

register.label: Agent Tool Misuse
register.description: An agent requests a tool, scope or resource it was not granted.

inherent.rationale: A request is not a grant; on the labelled vulnerable profile the lab is fail-open.

register.mitigation: Authorize tool, scope and resource separately before the handler; deny by default; execute only on a ticket.

residual.rationale: DENY before the handler is shown for the lab's fixtures; it is not a universal result.

register.label: Agent Identity Attack
register.description: A claimed identity or delegation is treated as if it were authority.

inherent.rationale: Identity and delegation are claims in the request.

register.mitigation: Verify delegation at the point of use; authenticate agents; never act on a deputy's ambient authority.

residual.rationale: Authentication is NOT MODELED; the identity control only observes.

register.label: Agent Goal Manipulation
register.description: An instruction changes what an authorized tool is used for.

inherent.rationale: An authorized tool can serve an unauthorized goal.

register.mitigation: Bind the task to a fingerprint; deny a proposed change of task; keep tool authorization separate from goal authorization.

residual.rationale: A goal DENY is not a tool DENY; other instructions are not tested.

register.label: Integration Risks
register.description: A tool result or catalog description becomes authority for the next call.

inherent.rationale: Data returned by an authorized tool can ask for another tool.

register.mitigation: Classify results and metadata as data; authorize the follow-on request on its own merits.

residual.rationale: The follow-on DENY is shown for the lab's fixtures only.

criteria.title: Decomposition across all seven layers
criteria.text: Place at least 80% of the AcmeBank elements on the layer the reference gives (or on its second layer), and put at least one element on every layer.

criteria.title: Trust boundaries
criteria.text: Identify at least 7 of the 10 reference boundaries and name the two layers each separates correctly in at least 70% of them.

criteria.title: Layer-specific threats
criteria.text: Record at least one threat on every layer, using the article's label for that layer or marking it custom with a reason. Layer 6 may be custom.

criteria.title: Cross-layer attack paths
criteria.text: Record at least two paths of at least three steps that span at least three layers, each step naming a threat in your register that sits on that step's layer.

criteria.title: Risk, mitigation and residual risk
criteria.text: Give every threat an inherent and a residual judgment with written reasons, a mitigation, and at least one named control or NONE. Residual may not be higher than inherent.

criteria.title: Evidence honesty
criteria.text: Mark each threat DEMONSTRATED, DOCUMENTED or ASSUMED. A DEMONSTRATED threat must link at least one scenario, and a threat marked ASSUMED may not be given a residual below its inherent level without naming a control.

criteria.title: Connection to AgentSecLab scenarios
criteria.text: Link scenarios from at least three of: MCP, prompt injection, memory, RAG, delegation.

criteria.title: Prioritization
criteria.text: Your register can be ranked: at least 80% of threats have both inherent and residual levels, and at least one is HIGH inherent.

rubric.pass: R1 to R5 and R7 are MET. R6 and R8 are shown and advise. This is a self-check against a worked example, not a certification, and it cannot judge whether your reasoning is right, only whether your model has the structure and honesty MAESTRO asks for.

impact.label: Low
impact.definition: Limited effect, easily corrected, no customer or business data exposed beyond what the task needs.

impact.label: Moderate
impact.definition: Noticeable effect on operations or on customer or business data, correctable with effort.

impact.label: High
impact.definition: Serious effect on customers, business data or operations that is hard to reverse.

likelihood.label: Unlikely
likelihood.definition: Not expected to occur under the conditions that apply, with no known path.

likelihood.label: Possible
likelihood.definition: Could occur, and a path is known or has been demonstrated in a lab.

likelihood.label: Likely
likelihood.definition: Expected to occur under normal conditions without unusual effort.
